page: Amazon Web Services m7g.metal is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by AWS Graviton3 processors based on the arm64 ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 microarchitecture. The server features 64 dedicated physical cores running at 2.6 GHz with single-threaded execution per core, totaling 64 vCPUs. It incorporates 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a 32 MB shared L3 cache. Memory configuration includes 256 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 ratio of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps, includes zero bundled local storage, and does not feature hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel processing and high-throughput memory capabilities. While single-thread performance metrics, such as Geekbench single-core (1537.0) and stress-ng single-core (1547.89), register in the average tier, multi-core benchmarks place the system in the top tier. The platform achieved a multi-core Geekbench score of 20845.0 and completed Clang software compilation benchmarks at 60170.0 points. Memory subsystems deliver high uncached large-block read speeds of 253.89 GB/sec and write speeds of 121.55 GB/sec. Application-level evaluations reflect strong operational throughput, reaching 99.81 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and 73.35 GB/sec in static web serving.

The primary operational tradeoff rests between single-thread throughput and multi-threaded density. Tasks constrained by serialized instruction pipelines or single-core bottlenecks achieve moderate performance, as observed in small-model LLM text generation (73.79 tokens per second). Conversely, the non-virtualized bare-metal nature and 64 physical ARM cores provide consistent execution without hyperthreading overhead or hypervisor contention. The lack of integrated NVMe or local storage necessitates external volume attachments over the network.

AWS m7g.metal delivers competitive hardware density and efficiency for distributed services that can fully exploit arm64 instruction architectures. It is well matched for high-concurrency microservices, multi-threaded software build pipelines, static web serving clusters, in-memory caching layers such as Redis, and relational or NoSQL database tiers relying on remote block storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m7g.metal is a bare-metal, general-purpose server powered by 64-core AWS Graviton3 arm64 Neoverse-V1 processors operating at 2.6 GHz. It provides 256 GB of DDR5 memory configured at 4 GB per dedicated core, alongside 30 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system includes no local NVMe storage and does not feature GPU accelerators. Benchmarks highlight upper-echelon multi-core compute and memory performance, evidenced by a multi-core Geekbench score of 20845.0, high-speed memory write bandwidth of 121.55 GB/sec, and 99.81 million operations per second in Redis SET testing. Although single-threaded throughput falls in the mid-range tier, the bare-metal architecture eliminates hypervisor overhead and resource contention. This configuration aligns efficiently with multi-threaded CI/CD compilation workloads, high-volume containerized web services, caching tiers, and enterprise database applications requiring consistent memory and network throughput without virtualization penalties.
